title: "CEF Cheat Sheet"
---

## bash

Get a directory's total size in MB and file count. (coreutils 9.4; findutils 4.9.0; gawk 5.2.1)

```bash
dir_path="/path/to/directory"
printf "%.2f MB (%s files)\n" \
  "$(du -sb "$dir_path" | awk '{print $1 / 1024 / 1024}')" \
  "$(find "$dir_path" -type f | wc -l)"
```

Remove specific files (and preview)
```bash
# Build reusable find arguments for the workflow_outdir_eval directory.
args=(
  -H workflow_outdir_eval  # Search this directory and follow command-line symlinks.
  -type d                 # Match directories.
  -name .cache            # Match directories named .cache.
  -prune                  # Do not descend into matched .cache directories.
  -o                      # Otherwise, evaluate the next expression.
  -type d                 # Match directories again for the alternate branch.
  -name FIMBench           # Match directories named FIMBench.
  -prune                  # Do not descend into matched FIMBench directories.
)
# Search recursively while pruning .cache and FIMBench directories from traversal.
find "${args[@]}" -print                  # Preview every matched path.
find "${args[@]}" -exec rm -rf -- {} +    # Remove every matched path in batches.
```

### System information

Get the current user name. (coreutils 9.4)

```bash
id -un
```

Get the operating system, kernel release, and architecture. (coreutils 9.4)

```bash
uname -srm
```

Restart the system. (systemd 255.4)

```bash
sudo reboot
```

## Git

Keep the file on disk while removing it from Git tracking. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git rm --cached <file>
```

Undo the most recent unpushed commit while keeping changes staged. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
```

Create and push an annotated tag. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git tag -a v2026.08.21 -m "v2026.08.21"
git push origin --tags
```

Restore `smk/readme_eval.md` from a remote branch into the current working tree. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git restore --source=remotes/origin/64-viirs-prewarp-blocks -- smk/readme_eval.md
```

List local and remote branches. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git branch -a
```

Merge without committing, then abort if needed; a fast-forward creates no merge commit. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git merge --no-commit <branch>
git merge --abort
```

Apply a specific commit to the current branch. (Git 2.43.0)

```bash
git cherry-pick 1dd0d9bd9e50e41e6d9d7dfc25326155cbb77800
```

## tmux

Create or attach to a tmux session. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux new -s session_name
tmux attach -t <session-name>
```

Detach from the current tmux session by pressing `Ctrl+b`, then `d`. (tmux 3.4)

List all tmux sessions. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux list-sessions
```

List the windows in a tmux session. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux list-windows -t session_name
```

Switch to a specific window in a tmux session. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux select-window -t session_name:window_name
```

Kill a specific window in a tmux session. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux kill-window -t session_name:window_name
```

Stop every tmux session on the host. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux kill-server
```

Stop one tmux session. (tmux 3.4)

```bash
tmux kill-session -t NFHL_process
```


## GitHub

Rerun failed jobs for a GitHub Actions workflow run. (GitHub CLI 2.45.0)

```bash
gh run rerun --failed
```

## tar

Create a tarball without compression. (GNU tar 1.35)

```bash
tar -cf archive.tar path/to/files
```

Create a highly compressed tarball with Zstandard; GeoTIFFs may already be internally compressed, so size reduction can be modest. (GNU tar 1.35; Zstandard 1.5.5)

```bash
tar -I 'zstd -19' -cf archive.tar.zst path/to/files
```


## rsync

Interpret the `--itemize-changes` (`-i`) flags shown before each path. (rsync 3.2.7)

- The complete format is `YXcstpoguax`.
  - `Y`: update type.
    - `c`: a local change or creation occurred.
    - `.`: the item was not updated.
    - `*`: the remaining output contains an rsync message.
  - `X`: item type.
    - `f`: file.
    - `d`: directory.
    - `L`: symlink.
    - `D`: device.
  - `cstpoguax`: changed attributes, in order.
    - `c`: checksum or file value.
    - `s`: size.
    - `t`: modification time.
    - `p`: permissions.
    - `o`: owner.
    - `g`: group.
    - `u`, `n`, or `b`: access time, create time, or both.
    - `a`: ACL.
    - `x`: extended attributes.
    - `+`: the attribute is new or not applicable.
- Examples:
  - `cd+++++++++ ./`: rsync created the directory `./`.
  - `cd+++++++++ build_workflows/`: rsync created the directory `build_workflows/`.
